chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Khalaf ibn Hammad, from Zakariyya ibn Ibrahim, raising it, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in a hadith of his,
that he said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'The one who trusts an untrustworthy one, so there is no argument for him upon Allah.'

key_terms.غَيْرَ مُؤْتَمَنٍ: untrustworthy one / one not worthy of trust

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of trusting an untrustworthy person?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'hujjah' (divine accountability or excuse) is linked to the prudence of one's choices, implying that negligence in selecting a trustworthy agent constitutes a self-inflicted liability. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that individuals are responsible for the due diligence they exercise in delegating authority, thereby precluding them from blaming Allah for the resulting loss or consequence.
